entities.summary: Francesco Solari was an Italian sculptor, architect and engineer of the 15th century, born in Milan around 1420 and died in 1469 in Florence. He trained under the renowned artist Donato Bramante and later collaborated with the architect Antonio da Sangallo the Younger. Solari's most notable works include the bronze doors of the Milan Cathedral and the architectural designs for the Florence Cathedral. His contributions to Renaissance architecture and art were significant, influencing the development of the Italian Renaissance style. Solari's legacy can be seen in the works of later artists and architects, including Michelangelo and Bernini. The sculptor's innovative use of perspective and his ability to balance form and function made him a master of his craft. He is also notable for his work on the design of the Palazzo Vecchio in Florence, which showcased his expertise in creating functional and aesthetically pleasing buildings. Solari's work had a lasting impact on the development of Renaissance art and architecture, and he remains one of the most important figures of the 15th century.
